title: Ye’s Chicago Homecoming: The 7 Best Moments From Night 2
summary: It was one for the history books at Soldier Field.
contentText:
Ye (formerly Kanye West )’s two-night homecoming at Soldier Field served as a love letter to Chicago. Friday’s (Sept. 4) spectacle celebrated West’s legacy, influence and family tree touching three different decades.

The show was a star-studded affair, bringing 15 guests into the fold for a loaded, 60-track setlist that spanned about three hours. While past tours have been filled with rants and streams of consciousness, Ye kept the talking in between tracks to a minimum Friday night, running through hit after hit and inviting a range of collaborators to share the globe-shaped stage with him.

Every Guest Ye Brought Out During Night 2 of His Star-Studded Homecoming Show in Chicago

After a destructive few years filled with antisemitic rants and outbursts, Ye has largely walked a straight path since taking out a full-page ad in The Wall Street Journal in January apologizing for his actions.

The damage has left him taking an unconventional route when it comes to touring, as he’s partnered with independent touring company IKON Presents for select stadium dates throughout 2026, which will continue with shows in Dallas, Houston and Phoenix later this year.

More than 70,000 fans laced up their Yeezys and donned tour merchandise over the past two days in Chicago, showing many are willing to overlook Ye’s controversial past — including his superstar friends that joined him on stage.

From The College Dropout to Bully , there was something for every generation of Ye fan. Day ones celebrated a reunion with those instrumental to the early success of Yeezy, like GLC, Consequence, Really Doe and Twista, while others moshed to appearances from the Cactus Jack family, such as Travis Scott and Don Toliver, both of whom have been open about Ye’s impact on their own careers.

It’s impossible to predict what the future holds for an artist as mercurial as West, but it’s clear there’s a path for him back into America’s mainstream, even if some choose to continue to ignore him in plain sight.
